label: OSFP 800GBASE-FR4 2 km
notes: The 800G rung, and the first row above 400G. Figures are the per-lane values FS prints for its OSFP-FR4-800G module (III. Optical Characteristics), a module the sheet states is compliant with IEEE 802.3dj D1p2's 800GBASE-FR4 optical interface: average launch power each lane -2.2..+4.9 dBm, average receive power each lane -6.2..+4.9 dBm, receiver sensitivity (OMAouter) -3.7 dBm, receive power (OMAouter) maximum +4.8 dBm, damage threshold +5.9 dBm, total average launch power +10.9 dBm. Four CWDM lanes at 1271 / 1291 / 1311 / 1331 nm carry 200G each over ONE duplex pair, which is why this row fits the link model: a leg is a duplex pair, and FR4 spends it on four wavelengths. The DR8 800G form puts eight lanes on eight fibres behind an MPO-16 (or twin MPO-12), which this model expresses: link.design carries fibres per leg and its BOM refuses a cable too thin for the count, and the budget is a per-lane launch-versus-receive subtraction, which is the right arithmetic for independent lanes. It is a row of its own, osfp-800g-dr8-500m (added 2026-11-28), rather than an exception to this one - this row previously said no parallel-lane 800G row could exist, and qsfp-dd-400g-dr4-500m's own note already told its caller to design with fibres: 8. The row keeps the AVERAGE receive minimum (-6.2), not the OMA sensitivity (-3.7), for the reason every class row here does: a launch figure is subtracted from an average receive figure, and the 2.5 dB between the two is the OMA-to-average conversion, not slack - so the class is -2.2 - (-6.2) = 4.0 dB. The row says 1310 nm because the engine budgets one wavelength and the cable's 1310 window publishes attenuation; per-lane figures are worst-lane. That 4.0 dB makes this the joint-tightest budget in the catalogue, tied with 100GBASE-FR1, and the same reading applies: 2 km x 0.35 dB/km = 0.7 dB of fibre plus the engine's default two SC/APC matings at 0.3 dB = 1.3 dB of ODN, 2.7 dB of headroom, which is under the 3 dB margin, so a compliant 2 km span reads fail (measured); 1 km is 0.95 dB and 3.05 dB, marginal; 500 m is 0.775 dB and 3.23 dB, marginal; a 0 dB patch is 0.6 dB and 3.4 dB, marginal (all measured, both directions). With two terminations it never reads ok, because ok needs 5 dB of headroom (margin plus the engine's 2 dB marginal band) and the 4.0 dB class cannot supply it - lower marginDb to about 1.5 dB if a project genuinely builds at this class, and take 800GBASE-2FR4/LR-class optics when a span has to survive a repair loop. Overload is not a trap here: the launch ceiling +4.9 dBm equals the receiver maximum +4.9 dBm, so a back-to-back pair with two connectors sits 0.6 dB under the point and needs no pad (measured: attenuator null, launch-window pad null). Reach and rate are still refused by name: the reach verdict binds at 2 km, and pairing this row with a 400G-FR4 head end throws 'the optics run at different rates (400000 and 800000 Mb/s)'. Two caveats the sheet prints itself: 802.3dj is a DRAFT, so a figure can move before the standard publishes, and the OMAouter table still carries TBDs for TDECQ, TECQ and stressed sensitivity. Replace the row with the optic actually purchased and its measured per-lane receive power before pricing a build.
